claim: A human TGFβ enhancer was identified that is specifically activated in melanoma cells treated with TGFB1 ligand.
source: Here we identified a human TGFb enhancer specifically activated in melanoma cells treated with TGFB1 ligand.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, and it is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Stable transgenic zebrafish were generated with the TGFβ Induced Enhancer driving green fluorescent protein (TIE:EGFP).
source: We generated stable transgenic zebrafish with this TGFb Induced Enhancer driving green fluorescent protein (TIE:EGFP).
evidence: The abstract states this directly, and methods describe the generation of the reporter line.

claim: TIE:EGFP was not expressed in normal melanocytes or early melanomas.
source: TIE:EGFP was not expressed in normal melanocytes or early melanomas but was expressed in spatially distinct regions of advanced melanomas.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by imaging data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E.

claim: TIE:EGFP was expressed in spatially distinct regions of advanced melanomas.
source: TIE:EGFP was not expressed in normal melanocytes or early melanomas but was expressed in spatially distinct regions of advanced melanomas.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by imaging data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing revealed that TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells down-regulated interferon response.
source: Single-cell RNA-sequencing revealed that TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells down-regulated interferon response while up-regulating a novel set of chronic TGFb target genes.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by scRNA-seq data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells up-regulated a novel set of chronic TGFβ target genes.
source: Single-cell RNA-sequencing revealed that TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells down-regulated interferon response while up-regulating a novel set of chronic TGFb target genes.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by scRNA-seq data in Figure 2C.

claim: ChIP-sequencing demonstrated that AP-1 factor binding is required for activation of chronic TGFβ response.
source: ChIP-sequencing demonstrated that AP-1 factor binding is required for activation of chronic TGFb response.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 2D-F and luciferase assays in Figure 2F.

claim: Overexpression of SATB2 showed activation of TGFβ signaling in early melanomas.
source: Overexpression of SATB2, a chromatin remodeler associated with tumor spreading, showed activation of TGFb signaling in early melanomas.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by imaging data in Figure 4A and 4D.

claim: Macrophages localize to TIE:EGFP+ regions in melanomas.
source: Confocal imaging and flow cytometric analysis showed that macrophages localize to TIE:EGFP+ regions and preferentially phagocytose TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells compared to TIE:EGFP- melanoma cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by confocal imaging in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Macrophages preferentially phagocytose TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells compared to TIE:EGFP- melanoma cells.
source: Confocal imaging and flow cytometric analysis showed that macrophages localize to TIE:EGFP+ regions and preferentially phagocytose TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells compared to TIE:EGFP- melanoma cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3D and qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Melanoma is the deadliest form of skin cancer.
source: Melanoma, arising from pigment producing melanocytes, is the deadliest form of skin cancer, with an estimated 100,640 new cases and 8,290 deaths in the United States in 2024 alone (Siegel et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Siegel et al., 2024.

claim: There were an estimated 100,640 new melanoma cases and 8,290 deaths in the United States in 2024.
source: Melanoma, arising from pigment producing melanocytes, is the deadliest form of skin cancer, with an estimated 100,640 new cases and 8,290 deaths in the United States in 2024 alone (Siegel et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Siegel et al., 2024.

claim: BRAFV600E is the most common mutation in melanoma, accounting for approximately 50% of melanoma cases.
source: The most common mutation in melanoma is BRAFV600E, which accounts for approximately 50% of melanoma cases and results in activation of the MAPK pathway promoting cell growth and survival (Akbani et al., 2015; Lo and Fisher, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Akbani et al., 2015 and Lo and Fisher, 2014.

claim: BRAFV600E results in activation of the MAPK pathway promoting cell growth and survival.
source: The most common mutation in melanoma is BRAFV600E, which accounts for approximately 50% of melanoma cases and results in activation of the MAPK pathway promoting cell growth and survival (Akbani et al., 2015; Lo and Fisher, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Akbani et al., 2015 and Lo and Fisher, 2014.

claim: Melanoma cells have increased expression and secretion of TGFβ ligands compared to normal melanocytes.
source: Melanoma cells have increased expression and secretion of TGFb ligands compared to normal melanocytes, and TGFb ligand expression correlates with melanoma progression (Van Belle et al., 1996; Albino et al., 1991; Rodeck et al., 1991; Rodeck et al., 1994; Krasagakis et al., 1998; Javelaud et al., 2008; Perrot et al., 2013; Rak et al., 1996; Cerami et al., 2012; Gao et al., 2013; Lauden et al., 2014; Schmid et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: TGFβ ligand expression correlates with melanoma progression.
source: Melanoma cells have increased expression and secretion of TGFb ligands compared to normal melanocytes, and TGFb ligand expression correlates with melanoma progression (Van Belle et al., 1996; Albino et al., 1991; Rodeck et al., 1991; Rodeck et al., 1994; Krasagakis et al., 1998; Javelaud et al., 2008; Perrot et al., 2013; Rak et al., 1996; Cerami et al., 2012; Gao et al., 2013; Lauden et al., 2014; Schmid et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: TGFβ ligand binding to receptors results in phosphorylation and activation of SMAD2 and SMAD3 transcription factors.
source: TGFb ligand binding to receptors on the cell surface results in phosphorylation and activation of SMAD2 and SMAD3 transcription factors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TGFβ signaling.

claim: SMAD2 and SMAD3 translocate to the nucleus with SMAD4 to modulate gene expression.
source: SMAD2 and SMAD3 translocate to the nucleus with SMAD4 to modulate gene expression (Batlle and Massagué, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Batlle and Massagué, 2019.

claim: In normal melanocytes and early melanoma, TGFβ acts as a tumor suppressor.
source: In normal melanocytes and early melanoma, TGFb acts as a tumor suppressor.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: In advanced melanoma, TGFβ is pro-tumorigenic as it induces growth, invasion, and metastasis.
source: However, in advanced melanoma TGFb is pro-tumorigenic as it induces growth, invasion, and metastasis (Perrot et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Perrot et al., 2013.

claim: TGFβ has an immunosuppressive effect in advanced tumors.
source: Generally, TGFb has an immunosuppressive effect in advanced tumors, resulting in inactivation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, expansion of immune suppressive regulatory T cells, inhibition of dendritic cell antigen presentation, and conversion of macrophages to an anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic M2-like state (Batlle and Massagué, 2019; Derynck et al., 2021; Naganuma et al., 1996; Ahmadzadeh and Rosenberg, 2005; Donkor et al., 2011; Fridlender et al., 2009; Mantovani et al., 2002; Standiford et al., 2011; Kobie et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: TGFβ results in inactivation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells.
source: Generally, TGFb has an immunosuppressive effect in advanced tumors, resulting in inactivation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, expansion of immune suppressive regulatory T cells, inhibition of dendritic cell antigen presentation, and conversion of macrophages to an anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic M2-like state (Batlle and Massagué, 2019; Derynck et al., 2021; Naganuma et al., 1996; Ahmadzadeh and Rosenberg, 2005; Donkor et al., 2011; Fridlender et al., 2009; Mantovani et al., 2002; Standiford et al., 2011; Kobie et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: TGFβ results in expansion of immune suppressive regulatory T cells.
source: Generally, TGFb has an immunosuppressive effect in advanced tumors, resulting in inactivation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, expansion of immune suppressive regulatory T cells, inhibition of dendritic cell antigen presentation, and conversion of macrophages to an anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic M2-like state (Batlle and Massagué, 2019; Derynck et al., 2021; Naganuma et al., 1996; Ahmadzadeh and Rosenberg, 2005; Donkor et al., 2011; Fridlender et al., 2009; Mantovani et al., 2002; Standiford et al., 2011; Kobie et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: TGFβ results in inhibition of dendritic cell antigen presentation.
source: Generally, TGFb has an immunosuppressive effect in advanced tumors, resulting in inactivation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, expansion of immune suppressive regulatory T cells, inhibition of dendritic cell antigen presentation, and conversion of macrophages to an anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic M2-like state (Batlle and Massagué, 2019; Derynck et al., 2021; Naganuma et al., 1996; Ahmadzadeh and Rosenberg, 2005; Donkor et al., 2011; Fridlender et al., 2009; Mantovani et al., 2002; Standiford et al., 2011; Kobie et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: TGFβ results in conversion of macrophages to an anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic M2-like state.
source: Generally, TGFb has an immunosuppressive effect in advanced tumors, resulting in inactivation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, expansion of immune suppressive regulatory T cells, inhibition of dendritic cell antigen presentation, and conversion of macrophages to an anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic M2-like state (Batlle and Massagué, 2019; Derynck et al., 2021; Naganuma et al., 1996; Ahmadzadeh and Rosenberg, 2005; Donkor et al., 2011; Fridlender et al., 2009; Mantovani et al., 2002; Standiford et al., 2011; Kobie et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: TGFβ can act as a chemoattractant for macrophages and monocytes to areas of inflammation.
source: TGFb can act as a chemoattractant for macrophages and monocytes to areas of inflammation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Recruitment of monocytes by TGFβ results in differentiation into macrophages that attach to the extracellular matrix or promote blood vessel leakiness allowing for tumor cell extravasation.
source: Recruitment of monocytes by TGFb results in differentiation into macrophages that attach to the extracellular matrix (ECM) or promote blood vessel leakiness allowing for tumor cell extravasation (Arwert et al., 2018; Kelly et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2021; Allen et al., 1990; Wahl et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In colorectal and urothelial cancers, TGFβ in the tumor microenvironment was found to mediate immune evasion such that TGFβ inhibition rendered these tumors susceptible to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors.
source: In colorectal and urothelial cancers, TGFb in the tumor microenvironment was found to mediate immune evasion such that TGFb inhibition rendered these tumors susceptible to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors (Tauriello et al., 2018; Mariathasan et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tauriello et al., 2018 and Mariathasan et al., 2018.

claim: Several TGFβ inhibitors are in clinical trials in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
source: Due to its immunosuppressive effect, several TGFb inhibitors are in clinical trials in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (Lan et al., 2018; Paz-Ares et al., 2020; Strauss et al., 2018; Martin et al., 2020; Welsh et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Following a 2-hr treatment of A375 cells with 10 ng/mL human recombinant TGFB1, 223 genes were significantly up-regulated (q<0.05) including typical TGFβ target genes SMAD7, JUNB, and PMEPA1.
source: RNA-sequencing indicated that following a 2-hr treatment of A375 cells with 10 ng/mL human recombinant TGFB1, 223 genes were significantly up-regulated (q<0.05) including typical TGFb target genes SMAD7, JUNB, and PMEPA1, while 94 genes were down-regulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, left).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Following a 2-hr treatment of A375 cells with 10 ng/mL human recombinant TGFB1, 94 genes were down-regulated.
source: RNA-sequencing indicated that following a 2-hr treatment of A375 cells with 10 ng/mL human recombinant TGFB1, 223 genes were significantly up-regulated (q<0.05) including typical TGFb target genes SMAD7, JUNB, and PMEPA1, while 94 genes were down-regulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, left).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis confirmed that TGFβ was the top up-regulated pathway following 2-hr TGFB1 treatment (q=0).
source: Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) of genes ranked by log2 fold-change (log2fc) confirmed that TGFb was the top up-regulated pathway following 2-hr treatment (q=0) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, right).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A 2-hr treatment with human recombinant TGFB1 ligand is sufficient to activate the TGFβ pathway.
source: This indicates that a 2-hr treatment with human recombinant TGFB1 ligand is sufficient to activate the TGFb pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RNA-seq and GSEA data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: TIE:EGFP reporter activity was significantly increased in the presence of ubi:caSMAD2 and ubi:caSMAD3.
source: TIE:EGFP reporter activity was significantly increased in the presence of ubi:caSMAD2 and ubi:caSMAD3, confirming that the reporter is inducible (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by electroporation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TIE:EGFP;Tg(mitfa:BRAFV600E);p53-/-;mitfa-/- stable embryos have EGFP expression in the anterior brain at 24 hr post fertilization.
source: TIE:EGFP;Tg(mitfa:BRAFV600E);p53-/-;mitfa-/- stable embryos have EGFP expression in the anterior brain at 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) extending along the brain and spinal cord beginning at 48 hpf (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TIE:EGFP expression extends along the brain and spinal cord beginning at 48 hpf.
source: TIE:EGFP;Tg(mitfa:BRAFV600E);p53-/-;mitfa-/- stable embryos have EGFP expression in the anterior brain at 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) extending along the brain and spinal cord beginning at 48 hpf (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The TIE:EGFP expression pattern is consistent with that previously found in a Smad3 zebrafish reporter.
source: This expression pattern is consistent with that previously found in a Smad3 zebrafish reporter, although in our hands this Smad3 reporter was not active in adults (Casari et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Casari et al., 2014.

claim: Treatment with TGFβ inhibitor SB431542 for 24 hr drastically reduced TIE:EGFP signal.
source: Treatment with this TGFb inhibitor for 24 hr drastically reduced TIE:EGFP signal (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: The TIE:EGFP reporter is specific to TGFβ signaling.
source: This indicates that the TIE:EGFP reporter is specific to TGFb signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the inhibitor treatment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Of the fish with melanoma formation (n=56), 55% turned on TIE:EGFP in advanced melanomas.
source: However, of the fish with melanoma formation (n=56), 55% turned on TIE:EGFP in advanced melanomas defined by protrusion from the body plane (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ cells often occur in clusters throughout the tumor.
source: TIE:EGFP+ cells often occur in clusters throughout the tumor and these cells are TIE:EGFP+ for many weeks at a time.
evidence: This is based on observations from imaging data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ cells are TIE:EGFP+ for many weeks at a time.
source: TIE:EGFP+ cells often occur in clusters throughout the tumor and these cells are TIE:EGFP+ for many weeks at a time.
evidence: This is based on observations from longitudinal imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Advanced zebrafish melanomas develop TGFβ responsive zones.
source: This data indicates that advanced zebrafish melanomas develop TGFb responsive zones.
evidence: This is an inference based on the imaging data showing TIE:EGFP expression in advanced melanomas.

claim: Approximately 2256 TIE:EGFP+ cells and 752 mitfa:mCherry+;TIE:EGFP- cells were sorted by flow cytometry for scRNA-seq.
source: Approximately 2256 TIE:EGFP+ cells and 752 mitfa:mCherry+;TIE:EGFP- cells (as a control) were sorted by flow cytometry for scRNA-seq.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2A.

claim: Melanoma cells were identified as being mitfa and sox10 positive.
source: In analysis of the scRNA-seq data, melanoma cells were identified as being mitfa and sox10 positive, while macrophages were identified as mpeg1.1 and marco positive.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2A and shown in the UMAP.

claim: Macrophages were identified as mpeg1.1 and marco positive.
source: In analysis of the scRNA-seq data, melanoma cells were identified as being mitfa and sox10 positive, while macrophages were identified as mpeg1.1 and marco positive.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2A and shown in the UMAP.

claim: Immediate-early TGFβ target genes were down-regulated in TIE:EGFPhigh cells.
source: We found that immediate-early TGFb target genes, identified following an acute 2 hr TGFB1 treatment in zebrafish melanoma cells, ZMEL1, were down-regulated in TIE:EGFPhigh cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 29 genes related to the extracellular matrix were up-regulated in TIE:EGFPhigh cells.
source: However, we identified 29 genes that were up-regulated in TIE:EGFPhigh cells. We termed these genes, related to the extracellular matrix, 'chronic' TGFb targets (Figure 2C; Katsuno et al., 2019; Verrecchia et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The top down-regulated pathways in TIE:EGFPhigh cells were interferon alpha and gamma.
source: Using GSEA analysis we found that the top down-regulated pathways in TIE:EGFPhigh cells were interferon alpha and gamma (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: TGFβ has an immune suppressive effect in these melanomas.
source: This suggests that TGFb has an immune suppressive effect in these melanomas.
evidence: This is an inference based on the down-regulation of interferon pathways in TIE:EGFP+ cells.

claim: SMAD2/3 bound regions are highly enriched for AP-1 motifs.
source: We found that these SMAD2/3 bound regions are highly enriched for AP-1 motifs (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by HOMER motif analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: ATF3 and JUNB were bound at 19% and 48% of SMAD2/3 responsive elements, respectively, before TGFB1 treatment was administered.
source: ATF3 and JUNB were bound at 19% and 48% of SMAD2/3 responsive elements, respectively, before TGFB1 treatment was administered.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: AP-1 factors, in particular JUNB, may be important for SMAD binding to chromatin.
source: This data indicates that AP-1 factors, in particular JUNB, may be important for SMAD binding to chromatin.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ChIP-seq data showing AP-1 binding prior to TGFB1 treatment.

claim: Loss of AP-1 site #1 rendered the enhancer region unresponsive to TGFβ signaling.
source: In A375 cells, loss of AP-1 site #1 rendered the enhancer region unresponsive to TGFb signaling, however loss of AP-1 site #2 did not alter inducibility (Figure 2F, bottom).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Loss of AP-1 site #2 did not alter inducibility of the enhancer.
source: In A375 cells, loss of AP-1 site #1 rendered the enhancer region unresponsive to TGFb signaling, however loss of AP-1 site #2 did not alter inducibility (Figure 2F, bottom).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: AP-1 site #1 is necessary for TGFβ inducibility at this enhancer.
source: This result indicates that AP-1 site #1 is necessary for TGFb inducibility at this enhancer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Deletion of the SMAD site destroyed TGFB1 responsiveness.
source: Deletion of the SMAD site also destroyed TGFB1 responsiveness.
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: AP-1 binding is required for responsiveness of this chronic TGFβ inducible enhancer in melanoma.
source: This data suggests that AP-1 binding is required for responsiveness of this chronic TGFb inducible enhancer in melanoma.
evidence: This is an inference based on the luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ macrophages express mitfa and sox10, suggesting recent phagocytosis of melanoma cells.
source: We identified TIE:EGFP+ macrophages in TIE:EGFP;Tg(mitfa:BRAFV600E);p53-/-;mitfa-/-;MCR:MCS melanomas that express mitfa and sox10, suggesting recent phagocytosis of melanoma cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Confocal imaging showed that the majority of a TIE:EGFP+ region of the tumor is composed of clustered TIE:EGFP+ macrophages.
source: Confocal imaging of these tumors showed that the majority of a TIE:EGFP+ region of the tumor is composed of clustered TIE:EGFP+ macrophages.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A subset of macrophages contain only puncta of TIE:EGFP signal, suggesting phagocytosis of TIE:EGFP+ cells.
source: Within these regions, we observed that a subset of macrophages contain only puncta of TIE:EGFP signal, suggesting phagocytosis of TIE:EGFP+ cells, while a separate subset are entirely yellow (suggesting endogenous reporter expression; Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A separate subset of macrophages are entirely yellow, suggesting endogenous reporter expression.
source: Within these regions, we observed that a subset of macrophages contain only puncta of TIE:EGFP signal, suggesting phagocytosis of TIE:EGFP+ cells, while a separate subset are entirely yellow (suggesting endogenous reporter expression; Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In 10 out of 13 tumors analyzed by confocal microscopy, about 60–80% of TIE:EGFP+ macrophages contained TIE:EGFP fragments.
source: In 10 out of 13 tumors analyzed by confocal microscopy, about 60–80% of TIE:EGFP+ macrophages contained TIE:EGFP fragments, while the remaining TIE:EGFP+ macrophages were diffusely TIE:EGFP+.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the remaining three tumors, about 30% of TIE:EGFP+ macrophages contained TIE:EGFP fragments.
source: In the remaining three tumors, about 30% of TIE:EGFP+ macrophages contained TIE:EGFP fragments, while the remaining were diffusely TIE:EGFP+.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In most tumors, the majority of TIE:EGFP+ macrophages are EGFP+ because they phagocytosed a TIE:EGFP+ cell.
source: Therefore, in most tumors (with rare exceptions), the majority of TIE:EGFP+ macrophages are EGFP+ because they phagocytosed a TIE:EGFP+ cell.
evidence: This is an inference based on the confocal imaging data showing EGFP fragments in macrophages.

claim: Macrophages were observed actively phagocytosing TIE:EGFP+ cells.
source: Indeed, we observed macrophages actively phagocytosing TIE:EGFP+ cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In three out of 13 tumors imaged by confocal microscopy, macrophages were engaged closely with a cluster of TIE:EGFP+;mitfa:BFP+ tumor cells, likely in the process of phagocytosis.
source: In three out of 13 tumors imaged by confocal microscopy, we observed that in TIE:EGFP+ patches, macrophages were engaged closely with a cluster of TIE:EGFP+;mitfa:BFP+ tumor cells, likely in the process of phagocytosis (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A large proportion of macrophages engulf a TIE:EGFP+ cell population that includes melanoma cells.
source: Together, this data reveals that a large proportion of macrophages engulf a TIE:EGFP+ cell population that includes melanoma cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the confocal imaging and scRNA-seq data.

claim: In all three tumors analyzed by flow cytometry, less than 1% of sorted cells were TIE:EGFP+.
source: In all three tumors, less than 1% of sorted cells were TIE:EGFP+, indicating this TGFb responsive population is rare.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The TGFβ responsive population is rare.
source: In all three tumors, less than 1% of sorted cells were TIE:EGFP+, indicating this TGFb responsive population is rare.
evidence: This is an inference based on the flow cytometry data showing less than 1% of cells are TIE:EGFP+.

claim: Macrophages phagocytose a significantly higher percentage of TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells compared to TIE:EGFP- melanoma cells.
source: Macrophages phagocytose a significantly higher percentage of TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells compared to TIE:EGFP- melanoma cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: qPCR showed that mitfa and sox10 expression is enriched in TIE:EGFP+ macrophages compared to TIE:EGFP- macrophages.
source: This was confirmed by qPCR, which showed that mitfa and sox10 expression is enriched in TIE:EGFP+ macrophages compared to TIE:EGFP- macrophages (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: SATB2 is amplified in 4–8% of melanoma patients.
source: The chromatin remodeler SATB2 is amplified in 4–8% of melanoma patients and its expression correlates with patient outcome.
evidence: This is stated in the text and is established knowledge from previous work.

claim: SATB2 expression correlates with patient outcome.
source: The chromatin remodeler SATB2 is amplified in 4–8% of melanoma patients and its expression correlates with patient outcome.
evidence: This is stated in the text and is established knowledge from previous work.

claim: SATB2 overexpression leads to accelerated melanoma onset, produces more aggressive, metastatic tumors, and induces a TGFβ signature.
source: Our lab has previously shown that SATB2 overexpression leads to accelerated melanoma onset, produces more aggressive, metastatic tumors, and induces a TGFb signature (Fazio et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fazio et al., 2021.

claim: Of the fish with SATB2 melanomas (n=27), 68% turned on TIE:EGFP in tumors.
source: Of the fish with SATB2 melanomas (n=27), 68% turned on TIE:EGFP in tumors, and its signal was expressed throughout the tumor volume (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: TIE:EGFP signal in SATB2 melanomas was expressed throughout the tumor volume.
source: Of the fish with SATB2 melanomas (n=27), 68% turned on TIE:EGFP in tumors, and its signal was expressed throughout the tumor volume (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ macrophages are not clearly polarized but express a combination of M1-like and M2-like marker genes.
source: We found that although TIE:EGFP+ macrophages are not clearly polarized, they express a combination of M1-like and M2-like marker genes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In TIE:EGFPhigh melanoma cells from SATB2 tumors, chronic extracellular matrix TGFβ target genes were up-regulated.
source: We found that in TIE:EGFPhigh melanoma cells, chronic extracellular matrix TGFb target genes were up-regulated and the top down-regulated pathways by GSEA again were interferon alpha and gamma (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The top down-regulated pathways in TIE:EGFPhigh melanoma cells from SATB2 tumors were interferon alpha and gamma.
source: We found that in TIE:EGFPhigh melanoma cells, chronic extracellular matrix TGFb target genes were up-regulated and the top down-regulated pathways by GSEA again were interferon alpha and gamma (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Down-regulation of interferon suggests that the TGFβ responsive melanoma cells likely evade adaptive immune responses, such as interferon-mediated antigen presentation to CD8+ T cells.
source: Down-regulation of interferon suggests that the TGFb responsive melanoma cells likely evade adaptive immune responses, such as interferon-mediated antigen presentation to CD8+ T cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the down-regulation of interferon pathways in TIE:EGFP+ cells.

claim: 40% of the MCR:SATB2 fish with melanomas (n=27) had TIE:EGFP expressed in early melanomas.
source: Finally, 40% of the MCR:SATB2 fish with melanomas (n=27) had TIE:EGFP expressed in early melanomas.
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 0% of MCR:MCS fish with melanomas (n=56) had TIE:EGFP+ early melanomas.
source: Meanwhile, 0% of MCR:MCS fish with melanomas (n=56) had TIE:EGFP+ early melanomas (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Overexpression of SATB2 leads to acceleration of TGFβ response in melanoma.
source: This shows that overexpression of SATB2 leads to acceleration of TGFb response in melanoma and suggests patients with this amplification may be more susceptible to TGFb inhibitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the imaging data showing early TIE:EGFP expression in SATB2 melanomas.

claim: Patients with SATB2 amplification may be more susceptible to TGFβ inhibitors.
source: This shows that overexpression of SATB2 leads to acceleration of TGFb response in melanoma and suggests patients with this amplification may be more susceptible to TGFb inhibitors.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that SATB2 overexpression leads to early TGFβ activation.

claim: TIE:EGFP is off in early melanoma but is expressed in most advanced melanomas.
source: TIE:EGFP is off in early melanoma but is expressed in most advanced melanomas, and remains on, reading out chronic TGFb signaling.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the imaging data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: TIE:EGFP remains on, reading out chronic TGFβ signaling.
source: TIE:EGFP is off in early melanoma but is expressed in most advanced melanomas, and remains on, reading out chronic TGFb signaling.
evidence: This is based on longitudinal imaging data showing persistent TIE:EGFP expression.

claim: TGFβ responsive melanoma cells down-regulate interferon.
source: These TGFb responsive melanoma cells down-regulate interferon, up-regulate a series of novel chronic TGFb target genes, and are preferentially phagocytosed by macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the scRNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TGFβ responsive melanoma cells up-regulate a series of novel chronic TGFβ target genes.
source: These TGFb responsive melanoma cells down-regulate interferon, up-regulate a series of novel chronic TGFb target genes, and are preferentially phagocytosed by macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the scRNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TGFβ responsive melanoma cells are preferentially phagocytosed by macrophages.
source: These TGFb responsive melanoma cells down-regulate interferon, up-regulate a series of novel chronic TGFb target genes, and are preferentially phagocytosed by macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the flow cytometry and confocal imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Once the TIE:EGFP reporter is activated, it may remain active because chromatin is held in an open state by epigenetic modifications or AP-1 factors.
source: Once the TIE:EGFP reporter is activated, it may remain active because chromatin is held in an open state by epigenetic modifications or AP-1 factors.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of chronic TGFβ signaling.

claim: AP-1 factors may be holding TIE chromatin open, therefore potentiating its ability to drive downstream reporter expression.
source: AP-1 factors may be holding TIE chromatin open, therefore potentiating its ability to drive downstream reporter expression.
evidence: This is speculation based on the ChIP-seq and luciferase data showing AP-1 binding is required for enhancer activity.

claim: AP-1 factors likely hold chromatin open for other TGFβ target genes to potentiate the TGFβ response.
source: Simultaneously, AP-1 factors likely hold chromatin open for other TGFb target genes to potentiate the TGFb response.
evidence: This is speculation based on the ChIP-seq data showing widespread AP-1 binding at SMAD2/3 responsive elements.

claim: AP-1 inhibitors could disrupt TGFβ induction.
source: This may allow for a rapid signaling response upon TGFb activation and suggests that AP-1 inhibitors could disrupt TGFb induction.
evidence: This is speculation based on the finding that AP-1 binding is required for TGFβ enhancer activity.

claim: Chronic TGFβ target genes degrade extracellular matrix, promoting migration.
source: Based on the literature, these targets degrade extracellular matrix, promoting migration (Verrecchia et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Verrecchia et al., 2001.

claim: Some of the chronic TGFβ targets were identified in one of the few reports of long-term TGFβ signaling in human mammary epithelial cells for 12 or 24 days.
source: Some of the chronic TGFb targets were identified in one of the few reports of long-term TGFb signaling in human mammary epithelial cells for 12 or 24 days (Figures 2C and 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and refers to data shown in Figures 2C and 4C.

claim: Prolonged TGFβ treatment was found to stabilize EMT, stem cell state, and drug resistance in breast cancer cells.
source: Prolonged TGFb treatment was found to stabilize EMT, stem cell state, and drug resistance in breast cancer cells (Katsuno et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Katsuno et al., 2019.

claim: A subset of melanoma patients exhibit up-regulation of chronic TGFβ target genes according to TCGA data.
source: According to TCGA data in cBioPortal, a subset of melanoma patients exhibit up-regulation of these genes (Cerami et al., 2012; Gao et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cerami et al., 2012 and Gao et al., 2013.

claim: The chronic TGFβ signature could be used as biomarkers to identify patients with chronic TGFβ signaling.
source: In the future, this signature could be used as biomarkers to identify patients with chronic TGFb signaling and these patients may benefit from treatment with TGFb inhibitors.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the findings.

claim: Patients with chronic TGFβ signaling may benefit from treatment with TGFβ inhibitors.
source: In the future, this signature could be used as biomarkers to identify patients with chronic TGFb signaling and these patients may benefit from treatment with TGFb inhibitors.
evidence: This is speculation about future therapeutic applications.

claim: Cancer cells are thought to circumvent the tumor suppressive effects of TGFβ via mutations or epigenetic modifications.
source: Cancer cells are thought to circumvent the tumor suppressive effects of TGFb via mutations or epigenetic modifications (Derynck et al., 2021; Kim et al., 2021; Massagué et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2017; Seoane and Gomis, 2017; Suriyamurthy et al., 2019; Miyazawa and Miyazono, 2017; Tang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Melanomas up-regulating SATB2 may overcome the tumor-suppressive effects of TGFβ signaling earlier in tumor development, leading to more aggressive and invasive melanomas.
source: It is possible that melanomas up-regulating the epigenetic regulator SATB2 may overcome the tumor-suppressive effects of TGFb signaling earlier in tumor development, leading to more aggressive and invasive melanomas (Fazio et al., 2021).
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that SATB2 overexpression leads to early TGFβ activation, supported by a citation to Fazio et al., 2021.

claim: Aggressive melanoma subtypes like SATB2, which activate TGFβ very early in melanoma development, would be most responsive to early intervention with TGFβ inhibitors.
source: It is expected that aggressive melanoma subtypes like SATB2, which activate TGFb very early in melanoma development, would be most responsive to early intervention with TGFb inhibitors.
evidence: This is speculation about therapeutic implications.

claim: The regionality of TGFβ response could occur due to gradients in the TGFβ morphogen, possibly induced by TGFβ signaling within tumor cells in particular regions of the tumor.
source: The regionality of TGFb response could occur due to gradients in the TGFb morphogen, possibly induced by TGFb signaling within tumor cells in particular regions of the tumor.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of regional TGFβ response.

claim: TGFβ can act as a chemoattractant for macrophages and induces an anti-inflammatory M2-like state.
source: As mentioned above, TGFb can act as a chemoattractant for macrophages and induces an anti-inflammatory M2-like state.
evidence: This is established knowledge stated in the introduction.

claim: Local TGFβ signaling within the tumor may influence macrophage localization and phagocytosis, likely leading to changes in their behavior.
source: This data suggests that local TGFb signaling within the tumor may influence macrophage localization and phagocytosis, likely leading to changes in their behavior.
evidence: This is speculation based on the confocal imaging and flow cytometry data.

claim: Serpine1 mRNA was differentially upregulated in TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells.
source: One factor we identified in our single cell RNA-seq data that may mediate this interaction is serpine1. Serpine1 mRNA was differentially upregulated in TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells, and its receptor, lrp1ab was expressed on TIE:EGFP+ macrophages (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the text based on scRNA-seq data.

claim: The receptor for serpine1, lrp1ab, was expressed on TIE:EGFP+ macrophages.
source: One factor we identified in our single cell RNA-seq data that may mediate this interaction is serpine1. Serpine1 mRNA was differentially upregulated in TIE:EGFP+ melanoma cells, and its receptor, lrp1ab was expressed on TIE:EGFP+ macrophages (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the text based on scRNA-seq data.

claim: SERPINE1 has been shown to promote cancer cell invasiveness and macrophage recruitment in an esophageal squamous cell carcinoma model.
source: SERPINE1, which encodes plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), has been shown to promote cancer cell invasiveness and macrophage recruitment in an esophageal squamous cell carcinoma model (Sakamoto et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sakamoto et al., 2021.

claim: TIE:EGFPhigh macrophages differentially express mmp14b and the cysteine protease legumain.
source: TIE:EGFPhigh macrophages differentially express mmp14b and the cysteine protease legumain, both of which have been described to promote TGFb bioavailability (Bai et al., 2019; Sounni et al., 2010; Robertson and Rifkin, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text based on scRNA-seq data, supported by citations.

claim: mmp14b and legumain have been described to promote TGFβ bioavailability.
source: TIE:EGFPhigh macrophages differentially express mmp14b and the cysteine protease legumain, both of which have been described to promote TGFb bioavailability (Bai et al., 2019; Sounni et al., 2010; Robertson and Rifkin, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bai et al., 2019; Sounni et al., 2010; Robertson and Rifkin, 2016.

claim: Macrophages may be recruited to TIE:EGFP+ regions by PAI-1 gradients.
source: Together, these preliminary transcriptional data may indicate a mechanism by which macrophages are recruited to TIE:EGFP+ regions by PAI-1 gradients.
evidence: This is speculation based on the scRNA-seq data showing serpine1 expression.

claim: Recruited macrophages may phagocytose TIE:EGFP+ tumor cells and then go on to amplify the pool of active, bioavailable TGFβ through the activity of enzymes such as mmp14b and lgmn.
source: Recruited macrophages may phagocytose TIE:EGFP+ tumor cells and then go on to amplify the pool of active, bioavailable TGFb through the activity of enzymes such as mmp14b and lgmn.
evidence: This is speculation based on the scRNA-seq data showing expression of these enzymes.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ macrophages may be transitioning from the M1-like to the M2-like phenotype.
source: This may indicate that a transition is occurring from the M1-like to the M2-like phenotype.
evidence: This is speculation based on the scRNA-seq data showing mixed M1 and M2 marker expression.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ macrophages have higher expression of cholesterol and fatty acid genes compared to TIE:EGFP- macrophages.
source: Preliminary evidence comparing the transcriptional signatures of macrophages in the SATB2 expressing tumor indicates that TIE:EGFP+ macrophages have higher expression of cholesterol and fatty acid genes (i.e. abca1a, npc2) as well as apoptotic genes (i.e. casp3b, caspa) compared to TIE:EGFP- macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on scRNA-seq data.

claim: TIE:EGFP+ macrophages have higher expression of apoptotic genes compared to TIE:EGFP- macrophages.
source: Preliminary evidence comparing the transcriptional signatures of macrophages in the SATB2 expressing tumor indicates that TIE:EGFP+ macrophages have higher expression of cholesterol and fatty acid genes (i.e. abca1a, npc2) as well as apoptotic genes (i.e. casp3b, caspa) compared to TIE:EGFP- macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on scRNA-seq data.

claim: Intrinsic TGFβ signaling or phagocytosis of TIE:EGFP+ cells may induce a stress phenotype within macrophages, resulting in death.
source: This indicates that intrinsic TGFb signaling or phagocytosis of TIE:EGFP+ cells may induce a stress phenotype within macrophages, resulting in death.
evidence: This is speculation based on the scRNA-seq data showing increased apoptotic gene expression.

claim: Death of macrophages over time would allow the tumor cells to evade phagocytosis.
source: In this case, death of macrophages over time would allow the tumor cells to evade phagocytosis.
evidence: This is speculation about the consequences of macrophage death.

claim: β-2-microglobulin (b2m) is one of the top down-regulated genes in TIE:EGFP expressing melanoma cells.
source: Moreover, the interferon target gene, β–2-microglobulin (b2m) is one of the top down-regulated genes in TIE:EGFP expressing melanoma cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Loss of B2M is a known mechanism of immunotherapy resistance.
source: Loss of B2M, part of the MHC Class I molecules, is a known mechanism of immunotherapy resistance (Alavi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Alavi et al., 2018.

claim: Activation of TGFβ in melanoma is immunosuppressive, potentially by way of interferon modulation and effects on macrophage behavior.
source: Together, this data suggests that activation of TGFb in melanoma is immunosuppressive, potentially by way of interferon modulation and effects on macrophage behavior and supports the need for more work on combination TGFb and immune checkpoint inhibitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the scRNA-seq and imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There is a need for more work on combination TGFβ and immune checkpoint inhibitors.
source: Together, this data suggests that activation of TGFb in melanoma is immunosuppressive, potentially by way of interferon modulation and effects on macrophage behavior and supports the need for more work on combination TGFb and immune checkpoint inhibitors.
evidence: This is speculation about future research directions.

claim: Melanocyte development is conserved between zebrafish and mammals.
source: Melanocyte development is conserved between zebrafish and mammals (Mort et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mort et al., 2015.

claim: MITF is the master regulator of the melanocyte lineage and is conserved in zebrafish (mitfa).
source: The master regulator of the melanocyte lineage, MITF, is conserved in zebrafish (mitfa) and required for melanocyte development (Lister et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lister et al., 1999.

claim: Expression of mitfa:BRAFV600E together with a homozygous p53 missense mutation leads to development of zebrafish melanomas.
source: Expression of mitfa:BRAFV600E together with a homozygous p53 missense mutation, leads to development of zebrafish melanomas (Patton et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2005.
